title: Musk Says Terrafab Plant Will ‘Make Chips Better Than Anyone’
source_used: Bloomberg, read on The Edge Malaysia copy
key_facts: Elon Musk told customers and investors at the X Takeover event outside Tesla's Austin factory, by livestream on Saturday 10 Oct 2026, that his companies would probably 'figure out how to make chips better than anyone'.
He said he currently has 'no idea how to make microchips' and that it might take 'quite a few years'.
He said that on visits to competitors' plants he had not seen much customised equipment, which his companies have a lot of experience making.
Terrafab is planned for Grimes, Texas, as a joint venture of Tesla and SpaceX with Intel, with an initial investment of more than US$15 billion.
The project is expected to create 3,000 jobs and to receive a US$30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant.
The facility will be built in phases on about 3,000 acres; SpaceX controls more than 13,000 acres.
quote_evidence: “I don’t want to be complacent or entitled or anything, but, I think probably we’ll figure out how to make chips better than anyone. Honestly. I don’t know how long it’s going to take us to do that. It might take us quite a few years.”

Musk is preparing to build a Terrafab factory in Grimes, Texas, via a joint venture between his companies Tesla and SpaceX alongside Intel Corp, with an initial investment of more than US$15 billion (RM61.28 billion).
The project, which is expected to create 3,000 jobs, will receive a Texas Enterprise Fund grant of US$30 million.
why_it_matters_hint: A big chip-plant plan, but Musk's own words are hedged and the timetable open.
notes: Bloomberg returned 403; the text was read on The Edge Malaysia (https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/821386), which carries Bloomberg's story. Business Standard and Investing.com also carry versions.
